_comment:
'As an additional cost to play Cross the Line, you may **charge** your hero's soul.' Light Warrior Action - Attack; yellow printing, word-for-word identical to the red/blue siblings .drafts/cross_the_line_red.json and .drafts/cross_the_line_blue.json, whose verified shape this copies (no amount differs between printings).

COST, NOT EFFECT: 'as an additional cost to play' is additional_cost on the PLAY ability - a cost can block the play, an effect cannot. Shape copied from shipped dtd/beaming_bravado_yellow.json / dtd/light_the_way_red.json (the same sentence family; '27 cards share this shape' per the CHARGE handler's own comment) and the sibling drafts; all prove the spelling compiles.

CHARGE cost handler (cost_types.py:266-318) READS amount and optional/may - verified this session. With optional truthy, can_pay returns True unconditionally so the optional cost NEVER blocks the play (that is the printed 'you may'), and pay asks which hand card to charge via ask_optional, then routes through canonical effect_keywords.charge (CR 8.5.29), stamping the charged card's colour on the played card (dsl_charged_color). Cross the Line has no 'charged this way' payoff, so the stamp is simply unused.

BOOLEAN true, NOT the string "TRUE": this branch does bool(params.get("optional")) (cost_types.py:280), so ANY non-empty string - including "FALSE" - would read as optional. The corpus precedent authors a real boolean; copied that. (A mandatory cost would omit the key entirely.)

PRINTED KEYWORD 'Charge' NOT RE-AUTHORED as behaviour: triggers.py maps keyword 'charge' to `pass  # Card-specific - charge conditions vary per card` - the DB keyword is deliberately inert and this additional_cost is the only implementation, so authoring it here is not double-charging.

EMPTY effects list is intentional and compiles: the charge IS the whole card; beaming_bravado's comment records that an ability carrying only a cost 'compiles fine and resolves as a no-op'. The card being an Attack action is engine business (it attacks when played); no ATTACK effect is authored for attack action cards.
